adele: Quick heads-up — after the canary yesterday we saw a 12–18% P99 regression on the Llama-variant suite when routing to the 'fast-kernel' selector. Root looks like kernel selection differences across GPUs + driver image drift. Sharing notes and profiler snippets below.

omar: ugh. which GPUs and drivers? sounds like the usual CUDA drift hell.

adele: H100(e) vs A100. Canary ran on H100-prod (CUDA 12.2, driver 535.xx) while our replay harness mostly targets A100 images (CUDA 11.8, driver 510.xx). Kernel selector apparently favored a radix-based matmul on H100 that regresses for our seqlen distribution.

jin: can you paste the profiler output? also did the batching window change?

adele: sure — pasted the trimmed perf section:
```
Profile summary (trace id: 0x7f2):
- avg token latency: 8.7ms -> 10.2ms (canary vs baseline)
- P95: 23ms -> 27ms
- kernel chosen: matmul_radix_v2 (H100) vs matmul_tiled_v5 (A100)
- batch size distribution: same client loads, batching window ~12ms
- KV cache hit ratio: 98.7% -> 96.1% (small churn observed)
```

marta: KV drop to 96% could explain some extra mem copies. where are we seeing the copies? device <-> host?

adele: profiler shows an extra memcpy D2H stage on the H100 trace for sequences longer than 512. Looks like the chosen kernel requires a layout transform that triggers a staging buffer.

benchbot: perf regression classification: likely stage=kernel_selector (45%), memory_layout (30%), batching heuristic (15%), fallback/other (10%).

omar: If the kernel needs a layout transform that's expensive for long sequences, selector should be able to consider amortized cost vs latency SLO. Are we weighting by median seq len?

jin: we currently score kernels by per-token exec time @ canonical seqlen buckets (32/128/512) and pick lowest avg. That ignores layout penalty for mixed sequences.

marta: idea: add a layout_penalty term estimated from bytes-copied * memcpy_bandwidth_estimate. Then recompute expected latency using observed seq_len distribution from replay harness.

adele: I sketched a quick config change to the selector policy:
```
selector_policy:
  score = avg_kernel_time + layout_penalty * p_layout
  p_layout = observed_fraction_requiring_layout(seqlen_hist)
  layout_penalty = bytes_moved / memcpy_bandwidth
```

omar: nice. also we should lock images+driver in the replay that we use for apples-to-apples. Right now replay runs on A100:cuda11 image while canary used h100:cuda12. Different kernels and cuBLAS heuristics.

jin: Agree. Next steps:
- Re-run replay harness on H100 image with same container tag used in canary (registry/redwood/runtime:stable-2026-02)
- Pin driver to 535.xx on test cluster
- Run synthetic traffic with a seeded mix (20% long >512, 60% medium, 20% short)
- Enable detailed nvprof capture for 50 traces

marta: add to that: record `nvidia-smi -q` and `cuda-installation` outputs + `ldd` of the runtime .so so we can diff symbol resolution (sometimes we accidentally pick newer cuBLAS).

adele: pasted quick command snippet:
```bash
# on test node
registry_image=registry.redwood/runtime:stable-2026-02
docker run --gpus all --rm -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 $registry_image /bin/bash -c '
  nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia.q && 
  cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version >> /tmp/nvidia.q && 
  LD_PRELOAD= /bin/true && 
  ldd /opt/redwood/runtime/lib/inference.so > /tmp/ldd.txt
'
```

benchbot: baseline captures stored: s3://ri-bench/h100/canary/1748498000/

omar: Also double-check kernel flags in the image: environment flags like `TF32_CUTOVER=1`, `ALLOW_FUSED_ATTENTION=0` can flip kernel choices.

jin: good point — we had `ALLOW_FUSED_ATTENTION` defaulting to `auto` which on H100 picks fused path that does layout transforms. Might be the culprit.

marta: quick mitigation: add a temporary override for the selector to prefer `matmul_tiled_v5` when observed-seqlen-mean > 200. That's conservative but buys time.

adele: I'll open a PR with the selector change + a canary to the replay harness to run on H100. PR will include experiment plan and perf dashboards to compare.

omar: please also include the kernel-level flamegraphs and the nvtx ranges — that'll make it obvious where memcpy is firing.

adele: will do. tagging @sre-oncall to schedule H100 nodes for the replay window (need 2 nodes x 4hr).

sre-oncall: noted. reserving h100-test-02 from 0400-0800 UTC tomorrow. ensure the image tag is exact.

jin: one more ask — can the replay harness emit per-request kernel decisions so we can correlate seqlen -> kernel -> latency? right now it's aggregated.

adele: yes, I'll add a csv dump: request_id, seqlen, kernel_name, chosen_layout, latency_ms, kv_hit. that'll be in the canary artifacts.

benchbot: checklist updated:
- [ ] pin driver/image for replay (adele)
- [ ] add layout_penalty to selector scoring (adele/jin)
- [ ] emit per-request kernel logs (adele)
- [ ] run H100 replay (sre-oncall)
- [ ] compare flamegraphs + nvprof (omar)

omar: if the layout penalty fix improves P99 by >6% on H100, we can roll it to canary. if not, we may need to change default kernel mapping table for H100.

marta: ok — let's aim for the replay tomorrow and sync after the results. :thumbsup:

adele: thanks all — will post results in this thread.

(benchbot): action: regression-ticket #INF-4921 created for follow-ups.
